scope: All units read: text for sense and metre, translation and word glosses against the text. The text was not compared with the source page.

items.issue: pūtanākopakaḥ was rendered “who dealt death to Pūtanā”; the word speaks of anger, not killing.
items.change: Now “who turned his wrath on Pūtanā”.
Now “tinkling bells”, as the word gloss already had.

items.issue: The page prints rukmaṇīrāgiṇe; the name is Rukmiṇī, and the word gloss already reads rukmiṇī-rāgiṇe. The spelling rukmaṇī does occur in some prints of this hymn, so it may be the source’s own.
options: A. Change the text to rukmiṇīrāgiṇe and log it in SOURCES.md as a correction.
B. Keep rukmaṇī as the source’s spelling and make the word gloss match it.
items.recommend: A, if the Wikisource page reads rukmiṇī or you are content to normalise; the meaning is not affected either way.

items.issue: daṇḍakāraṇyabhūpuṇyatākāraṇam ends in -kāraṇam (neuter) among masculine nominatives describing Rāghava; many prints read -kāraṇaḥ. Grammatical as it stands (kāraṇa is a neuter noun in apposition).
options: A. Keep the text as it is.
items.recommend: A: the page reading is defensible and is the source’s.
